Practice Guide 41 supplement 5 was updated on 25 June 2015.
The plan specification applies to England and Wales.
The supplement covers plans lodged for estate boundary approval.
The supplement covers plans lodged for estate plan approval.
A lodged plan must clearly show scale and orientation.
A lodged plan must be drawn to the scale stated on it.
A bar scale may be added to the plan.
A scale of 1:1250 may be satisfactory when individual plot boundaries remain clear.
Intricate or building-internal boundaries may require a larger scale.
Plans marked 'For Identification only' are not acceptable.
Plans marked 'Do not scale from this drawing' are not acceptable.
Plans bearing reliability disclaimers are not acceptable.
A changeable 'working drawing' disclaimer is not acceptable.
The plan must be based on an accurate survey.
The accurate survey must be plotted to the chosen scale.
Scaled distances must be accurate to 0.3 mm at map scale plus one part in one thousand of the measured distance.
At 1:500, the stated tolerance for 100 metres is 0.25 metres.
At 1:1250, the stated tolerance for 100 metres is 0.475 metres.
At 1:500, the stated tolerance for 200 metres is 0.35 metres.
At 1:1250, the stated tolerance for 200 metres is 0.575 metres.
At 1:500, the stated tolerance for 500 metres is 0.65 metres.
At 1:1250, the stated tolerance for 500 metres is 0.875 metres.
At 1:500, the stated tolerance for 1,000 metres is 1.15 metres.
At 1:1250, the stated tolerance for 1,000 metres is 1.375 metres.
Survey control stations should be located in safe areas.
Setting out and the final as-built survey should use the original survey datum.
Measurements must be shown in metric form.
The plan must show detail immediately outside the site's external boundaries.
The plan must clearly define the extent of every plot.
Separate parking spaces and garages must be included in plot definition.
Each plot must have an identifying number or reference.
External plot boundaries must be defined precisely.
Separate parcels belonging to one property should be distinguished.
Different letter prefixes may distinguish parcels sharing a plot number.
The guidance gives G46 as an example garage reference.
The guidance gives P46 as an example parking-space reference.
Buildings must be shown in their correct position on plots.
Access drives and pathways forming plot boundaries must be shown.
Estate common parts and rights of way should be clearly indicated.
One floor plan can usually suffice when multiple floors are co-extensive and identical.
The plan must distinguish each flat by reference number.
The plan must state the floor level of each flat.
Intricate boundaries through a building may require an inset plan.
Plans that fail the requirements can be rejected.
Printing a PDF to fit paper can reduce a correctly scaled plan.
The guidance recommends selecting no page scaling to avoid reduction.
The paper size may need changing to print without reduction.
Developing-estate Ordnance Survey mapping is normally at 1:1250.
Significant differences from Ordnance Survey mapping should be reported for investigation.
Registration services are intended to reduce costs for developers and HM Land Registry.
The services cover initial site registration through pre-sales and plot sales.
The guide states that there are no fees for these services.
Each registration service can be used independently.
Straightforward approvals are targeted within five working days.
Applicants are contacted within five days when problems arise.
The service standards state that supplied information will be guaranteed as accurate.
